create.name: Rabbi Simcha Raphael
create.bio:
Simcha Paull Raphael, a rabbi, psychotherapist and teacher, has devoted his life's work to bringing together Jewish tradition, psychology and the study of death and the afterlife. He was born in Quebec and studied at Concordia University in Montreal. In 1986 he received a PhD in psychology from CIIS, the California Institute of Integral Studies, and in 1990 Rabbi Zalman Schachter-Shalomi ordained him as a Rabbinic Chaplain. He has taught at Temple University, La Salle University and Bryn Athyn College and served as a spiritual director at the Reconstructionist Rabbinical College. In the Philadelphia area he works as a transpersonal psychotherapist, bereavement counsellor and spiritual director.

As founding director of the DA'AT Institute, which focuses on death awareness, advocacy and training, he gives lectures, scholar-in-residence weekends and professional trainings for clergy, hospice staff and caregivers. The topics include Jewish views of the afterlife, Kabbalah, death rituals and mourning. Jewish Views of the Afterlife, his best-known book, is now in a third edition. Later titles include The Grief Journey and the Afterlife, May the Angels Carry You, Living and Dying in Ancient Times and Spirits, Ghosts, & Dybbuks, and he has also published collections of poetry.

books.title: Jewish Views of the Afterlife
books.author: Simcha Paull Raphael
books.description: A survey of Jewish teachings on life after death from the Bible through rabbinic, medieval, Kabbalistic and Hasidic sources to modern times. This third, 25th-anniversary edition adds a chapter on Yiddish literature and reflects on what the tradition offers for care of the dying and bereaved.

books.title: The Grief Journey and the Afterlife: Jewish Pastoral Care for Bereavement
books.author: Simcha Paull Raphael
books.description: A short book that sets traditional Jewish mourning rituals alongside contemporary psychological understanding of grief. It also draws on Kabbalistic teachings about the soul's journey after death, for clergy, caregivers and mourners.

books.title: May the Angels Carry You: Jewish Prayers and Meditations for the Deathbed
books.author: Simcha Paull Raphael
books.description: A practical collection of traditional and contemporary Jewish prayers, meditations and readings for use at the bedside of someone who is dying. Written for families, caregivers and clergy.

books.title: Spirits, Ghosts, & Dybbuks: Afterlife Journeys in Yiddish Lore
books.author: Simcha Paull Raphael
books.description: A study of afterlife beliefs in Yiddish folk and literary culture, from wandering spirits and dybbuks to the stories of I. L. Peretz and Isaac Bashevis Singer. It expands a chapter first published in Jewish Views of the Afterlife.

books.title: Living and Dying in Ancient Times: Death, Burial, and Mourning in Biblical Tradition
books.author: Simcha Paull Raphael
books.description: An exploration of how the ancient Israelites approached dying, burial and the afterlife, as seen in the Hebrew Bible. It closes with reflections on what these practices can offer end-of-life care today.

books.title: Jewish End-of-Life Care in a Virtual Age: Our Traditions Reimagined
books.author: Dayle A. Friedman, David Levin, Simcha Paull Raphael
books.description: A collection of essays and liturgies, co-edited by Simcha Raphael, on caring for the dying and mourning together when people cannot gather in person. It offers clergy and caregivers new forms for traditional death and mourning rituals.

courses.title: Lectures, Workshops and Scholar-in-Residence Programmes
courses.description: Talks, study sessions, mini-courses and Shabbaton weekends for congregations and communities on Jewish afterlife teachings, Kabbalah, Torah and end-of-life wisdom, mourning and ethical wills. Programmes are arranged on request.

courses.title: Professional Development Training
courses.description: Experiential workshops and trainings for clergy, chaplains, hospice staff, counsellors, educators and burial society members on death, bereavement and spirituality. Offerings range from single presentations to multi-day intensives.

courses.title: Judaism and Mysteries of Life, Death, and the World Beyond: A Scholar-in-Residence Shabbaton (Wheeling, IL)
courses.description: A weekend of teaching with Simcha Raphael hosted by Shir Hadash in Wheeling, Illinois, co-sponsored by Shalom Memorial. It explores Jewish teachings on death, the afterlife and the world beyond.

free_resources.title: Sacred Texts: Afterlife, Ancestral Journeys and Holy Day Themes
free_resources.description: A library of free PDF study texts compiled by Simcha Raphael on Jewish afterlife teachings, end-of-life passages in Torah and holy day themes. Useful for personal study or group learning.

free_resources.title: Hasidic Deathbed Stories
free_resources.description: A free online essay retelling how Hasidic masters such as the Baal Shem Tov met death, drawn from his book and an earlier magazine article. It presents these tales as models of conscious dying.
